_note: Tightened 55 s re-telling of the airplane Short's beat order (island, crate, engine, then one part per problem). Wording is illustrative, not a transcript of the published video. Replace every `pos`/`size`/`kind` with real shapes when you build the 3D parts.
topic: How an airplane works, built one part at a time from a crate

hook.say: You're stranded on an island. You bolt a boat engine onto a wooden crate. Congratulations! You just built the world's worst airplane.

beats.say: It rolls, but it can't lift. So you strap a surfboard on each side. Those are wings.
beats.label: WING

beats.say: Now it flies, but the nose keeps dipping. A small horizontal wing on the tail holds it level.
beats.label: HORIZONTAL STABILIZER

beats.say: Then it swings left and right. So you add an upright fin, like the feathers on an arrow.
beats.label: VERTICAL STABILIZER
beats.analogy: like the feathers on an arrow

beats.say: Stable, but you can't steer. Flaps on the tail wing tilt the nose, and flaps on the wings roll it.
beats.label: ELEVATOR + AILERONS

beats.say: You land way too fast. Wing flaps that fold down add lift and drag, so you can slow down.
beats.label: FLAPS

beats.say: One last problem: fuel. Tanks inside the wings keep it flying a long way.
beats.label: WING FUEL TANK

payoff.say: You built an airplane. The seagull is not impressed.
payoff.title: YOU BUILT AN AIRPLANE.
payoff.subtitle: ONE PROBLEM AT A TIME

ask.say: Save this for the next time someone asks how planes fly.

original_element: The build itself: every part is added on screen to fix the exact problem the previous part caused.
